reading: the shipped prompt gets the model to answer `suspicious` almost always, so the prompt is a real cause of the abstentions. Scenario-agnostic verdict definitions (C, D) and, more so, a schema that removes the abstain option (E) stop that, but accuracy on DEV stays far below the always-malicious level: the model then calls most alerts `benign` (see TP recall in the tables). Few-shot (F) did not help. A few rows are errors (Ollama HTTP 500 or a 120 s timeout on a single case); they are counted as wrong, never replaced by a stub. The labels cap what rule and source can decide (label ceiling above), so the difference has to come from the event body, where this model shows little signal.
ram_note: qwen2.5:3b Q4_K_M, 2.17 GB resident per Ollama /api/ps, 0 VRAM (CPU-only). Other sessions' Docker load tests shared this laptop's CPU for most of these runs, so latencies are indicative only (p50 swings between about 10 s and 35 s for the same prompt).
repeats_reading: shipped prompt versus E: the min-to-max ranges do not overlap over 2 to 3 runs, but the Wilson intervals on 21 cases do overlap, so the gap is suggestive and not established; E versus E with default sampling overlap on both measures. Every variant stays below the always-malicious level on these cases, and a variant that gets 100% FP recall does so by calling nearly everything `benign`, which misses most real attacks (see TP recall). Each variant has only 1 to 3 runs on 21 cases (3 false positives), so these are coarse.
